ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover Newton's dissatisfaction with action-at-a-distance (with the same 1692-letter quote), a mechanical push-model tradition, Einstein's spacetime-curvature explanation and its incompleteness, modern entropic gravity via Carney's team, the "one of several ways"/heat-and-entropy framing, and the minority-view-but-persistent-and-testable framing. The push-model description is generic ("a constant storm of tiny, invisible particles") rather than naming ether particles/corpuscular streams/vortex pressures as the guideline does, and GT's substantial Carney quote is entirely absent (Carney is named, his ideas paraphrased, but no direct quote used). Resolved on review: Carney's name and general role are retained, and the paraphrase ("the pull you feel from the Earth is more like a swarm behavior...an orderly, macroscopic pattern that is the result of the chaotic, random motions of hidden individual parts") restates his GT quote's specific idea (a hidden thermal/statistical system randomly producing the normal gravity effects on average) almost point for point. The missing element is the exact quoted wording, not the idea or its source, so this does not fail core_content.

A Force Emerges:
**1:** Both sections cover the singularity-incompleteness point, the horizon-area/second-law and Hawking-radiation/temperature parallels, the holographic-principle analogy, and Jacobson's 1995 reversal (elaborated with more technical detail: heat flux, Unruh temperature, entropy-area relation). GT's actual closing Carney quote ("He turned black hole thermodynamics on its head...mystified...") is replaced by a quote attributed to Carney that does not appear anywhere in research.md under any phase -- an exhaustive search of the full scraped Quanta article (which contains every other Carney quote used across this batch) turns up no match. This reads as a fabricated quotation. The underlying idea (Jacobson's derivation confirms a deep gravity-heat connection) is still conveyed, so core_content is not failed on idea-coverage grounds; the fabrication itself is scored under research_anchoring, where fabrication is squarely in scope. The added one-line Verlinde-2010 mention is closely related and does not displace anything.

Apparent Attraction:
**1:** Both sections cover the two-models framing (with all four co-authors named, matching GT exactly for once), the qubit-lattice Model 1 with Carney's polarization quote, the order-pockets/entropy-maximization mechanism with an explicit inverse-square-law derivation, the nonlocal Model 2, and the energy-capacity mechanism. This is the most faithfully GT-matching rendition of this section seen in this batch, with no notable omissions.Strengths and Weaknesses:
**1:** Both sections cover the ad-hoc/fine-tuning critique, the proof-of-principle framing, the weak-field-only limitation, the equivalence-principle critique with Van Raamsdonk's quote (preserved verbatim), and the strong-field challenge with Brustein's quote (preserved verbatim). GT's counter-view paragraph is entirely unattributed here -- neither Erik Verlinde's name nor his quote appears -- but the underlying argument (weak fields might reveal statistical fluctuations, distinguishing entropic gravity from deterministic GR) is fully and specifically conveyed in the writer's own words. Verlinde's name and quote are the citation for this argument, not the argument itself, so their absence does not fail core_content (consistent with the resolution reached for an equivalent Bassi-attribution case elsewhere in this batch). The added Visser and quantum-coherence critiques are additions that do not displace anything.

Testing Entropic Gravity:
**1:** Both sections cover the opening Carney quote (rendered here via a different, verified-genuine quote from the golden paper's own abstract, conveying the same testability point), the superposition thought experiment, the model's collapse prediction, the objective-collapse-model connection with the mass-dependent-decoherence signature, and the tabletop-experiments prospect (elaborated with torsion-pendulum specifics). GT's closing Van Raamsdonk quote and name are both absent, but the underlying value-of-exploring-alternatives argument (valuable to explore alternatives even though holography remains the leading candidate) is fully and specifically conveyed in the writer's own words. As with the Verlinde case above, the missing name and quote are the citation, not the substance, so this does not fail core_content.
